rationale: The documented defaults conflict with configured fallbacks. Both policies are plausible; the supplied files do not establish which defaults represent intended behaviour.
⚠️ The references endpoint deliberately retrieves identifiers and effective dates using LocationLevelRefs. Its annotation incorrectly documents the full LocationLevels response model.
The comment and contract require supplied metadata to override extracted values. Reversed isEmpty conditions discard nonempty header values.
The omission default is explicitly true. Parsing an absent query value with Boolean.parseBoolean instead passes false to storage.
The scope mismatch is confirmed. Both scope names are coherent choices; no supplied authorization policy independently establishes the intended namespace.
The contract describes potentially multiple container specifications and an array response. The structured branch returns a single ToolContainerfile directly.
⚠️ Creation uses a dedicated project_name request DTO and validator. The contract reuses the Project resource model, including server-managed fields, and misnames the creation property.
The delete guard enforces a different scope from the contract. The supplied files do not independently establish which scope name is intended.
The non-plain additional descriptor promises a ToolDescriptor metadata wrapper. Its implementation returns the internal SourceFile directly instead.
The XML annotation references a schema explicitly describing comma-separated text. The dedicated XML serializer uses an offices wrapper, establishing the annotation's wrong format reference.
EditableMetaData includes labels and properties. The version-update DTO copies only name and description, silently dropping supported submitted metadata.
The helper intends supplied metadata to override extracted values, but reversed isEmpty conditions prevent nonempty names and descriptions from overriding anything.
The schema default and runtime binding explicitly disagree. The supplied files do not establish whether Python 2 or Python 3 should be the omission default.
Listing enforces hydra.warden.groups while the contract specifies hydra.groups. No independent supplied policy determines which scope namespace is correct.
The camelCase contract and snake_case bindings differ consistently. Neither naming convention is inherently wrong, and the supplied files do not resolve intended public names.
The contract explicitly defines the no-review case as a successful null-filled DTO. The service instead throws the exception carrying a 404 status.
The declared minimum is one. The resource enforces only the upper cap and sends zero unchanged to setMaxResults, omitting lower-bound validation.
Update selects and authorizes metadata.ID copied from the body, never the path rule identifier. This breaks the documented target-resource selection.
⚠️ The request uses formatted date strings and locale-aware parsing. The nested array example and LocalDate declaration misdescribe that wire representation.
The handled-request branch writes the 410 object without returning, then writes the ordinary request, producing two response payloads.
The documented lower limit is one. Math.min applies only an upper cap, allowing zero to reach the database maximum-result setting.
⚠️ The response deliberately exposes the numeric repository identifier through an int64 JSON field. The isolated string schema misdescribes that representation.
⚠️ The error map deliberately distinguishes rule violations from unprocessable schemas. The contract omits the latter's explicit 422 response.
Either absent bound makes the entire price predicate true, so a supplied lower or upper bound alone cannot perform its documented filter.
⚠️ The registered LocalDate serializer deliberately emits year/month/day arrays. The response-only string declaration fails to describe the serializer used by this endpoint.
The nested application's log lookup passes only log ID and timestamp. No selected-application comparison occurs before returning the globally retrieved log.
⚠️ The kind endpoint deliberately retrieves and serializes identifier/kind pairs with a dedicated DTO. Its annotation incorrectly advertises full Location objects.
⚠️ The request's dateFormat and locale accompany scalar date parsing. The submittedOnDate LocalDate declaration and array example describe the wrong request representation.
⚠️ Repayment-start dates use the request's formatted scalar date parser. The contract's array example contradicts that convention and its own dateFormat/locale fields.
After writing the handled-request 410 payload, the handler falls through to writing the ordinary logout request. The branch lacks a terminating return.
The advertised sorting field restrictions are not checked. generateSortable constructs a field directly from arbitrary input after removing only the descending prefix.
⚠️ Missing products deliberately raise NotFoundException mapped to 404, matching other product-not-found declarations within this contract. The list operation incorrectly groups that case under 400.
The member-addition scope mismatch is explicit. Neither the contract nor the guard supplies independent evidence resolving which scope name represents the intended policy.
The member-removal guard and contract use different scope names. Without an independent authorization policy, the intended name cannot be determined.
The handled-consent branch writes a 410 response but continues to serialize the ordinary consent request. A terminating return is missing.
Creation requires hydra.warden.groups in code and hydra.groups in the contract. The supplied evidence confirms disagreement without establishing the intended scope namespace.
⚠️ Business-date listing uses the registered LocalDate array serializer. The string response annotation misdescribes this deliberate year/month/day representation.
The selected API never reaches the single-log lookup. The service retrieves by global ID and timestamp, then returns the log without checking API ownership.
The route calls the unscoped alert-event overload. A supplied overload checks reference type and identifier, but the API route bypasses it.

The controller defaults absent public metadata but never validates nonempty values against the documented true/false set before copying them into the creation model. Downstream storage validation is not supplied.

⚠️ The implementation explicitly distinguishes incompatible content from an unprocessable schema and maps the latter to 422. The operation's response documentation omits that deliberate error category.
⚠️ The inherited API deliberately requires an expected hash for guarded reference reassignment. The OpenAPI query annotation omits that requiredness.
The contract's method signature itself returns SingleReferenceResponse, matching the implementation and wrapper DTO. Only its response schema incorrectly references bare Reference.
Explicit default years make omitted time bounds valid requests. The implementation instead uses requiredInstant for both bounds and provides neither promised default.
The single-ID operation retrieves one property, as does the correctly documented name lookup. Its response annotation incorrectly reuses the list-wrapper model.
The handler validates identifiers but dereferences status before checking it. A null status raises an unmapped exception instead of the declared invalid-request response.

⚠️ The supplied strategy replaces subjects only on an existing policy entry and rejects missing entries. Its documented 204 fits this operation; the additional collection-creation response appears inapplicable.
The annotation names snapshots while its own description, Java return type, and installed-package service all identify packages. The declared response model is wrong.
assetIds is explicitly optional in both interface and controller. Unlike other optional parameters, it receives no fallback before stream dereferences the nullable list.

requireNotNull throws for missing device_response before domain validation. The supplied handler's fold recovers validation errors but provides no exception handler translating that throw to the promised 400 body.
The successful creation response explicitly includes a SubmodelElement. The controller creates it but constructs the 201 ResponseEntity with status alone, omitting the required representation.
The blob endpoint documents a blob-id override but reads CLOB_ID. This is the wrong resource's query key, leaving the advertised override unused.
Creation extracts the supplied metadata, but its existing-artifact fallback drops those arguments and invokes an update overload with null name and description.
Duplicate errors reach the response writer without a local conflict conversion. However, the writer and underlying error mapping are absent, so the asserted final 500 cannot be established.
⚠️ Retrieval and formatting deliberately use the dedicated RecentValue model for recent observations. The response annotation incorrectly references the distinct Tsv model.
The supplied backend unconditionally appends the reference without checking existence, and the controller returns 201. Duplicate references bypass the documented conflict behavior.
An unknown server-side commit outcome is explicitly documented as 500. The mapper categorizes CommitStateUnknownException as a client bad request, losing that distinction.
⚠️ The configuration uses public-client as a boolean flag and resource as the client name. The schema incorrectly describes public-client itself as the name string.
⚠️ Annual interest is deliberately maintained as BigDecimal alongside fractional interest fields. An integer-only response declaration unnecessarily excludes valid fractional rates.

The model explicitly advertises _links but supplies only an unannotated getLinks getter. Swagger naming alone does not implement the promised JSON property rename; serializer configuration is not supplied.
The route deliberately converts membership roles to a scope/name map in GroupMemberEntity. Its annotation incorrectly references the unconverted MemberEntity model.
⚠️ Water-user, contract, accounting, and pump routes consistently use the singular water-user segment. The isolated water-users annotation misstates the registered resource hierarchy.
The operation explicitly promises 204 for a successful bodyless update. The controller performs the update but constructs a 200 response instead.
The upload success contract specifies 204. After storing the file, the controller returns an empty 200 response rather than the declared update status.
The creation route differs in segment order between contract and controller. Both structures are plausible; the supplied files do not establish the intended public route.
The single-basin operation wraps the retrieved object in a singleton list before formatting. That introduces collection structure where the contract promises one basin.
The contract explicitly classifies an unknown server-side commit outcome as 500. The mapper returns 400 for that exception, incorrectly presenting a server failure as invalid client input.
A 204 response has no response body. The void deletion method fits that status; the contract's attached RoleEntity content declaration is contradictory.

Error entries are emitted deliberately, but OffsetRecordSent requires neither partition nor offset and permits additional properties. The supplied schema therefore does not itself establish a violation or identify the defective artifact.
The contract's own example maps event names directly to booleans, matching the command model. Its extra nested-map type is erroneous.
⚠️ Permission selection is explicitly processed as boolean flags and returned as boolean changes. The documentation model declares those flags as strings instead.
⚠️ Both format converters deliberately preserve an absent Kafka value as JSON null. The shared ConsumerRecord schema fails to allow this supported null representation.
⚠️ Reference deletion deliberately requires the expected hash through inherited validation. The OpenAPI query parameter fails to declare this concurrency precondition as required.
⚠️ Merge validation explicitly requires the target's expected hash, independently of the optional source hash. The query annotation omits that required target concurrency precondition.
The allowed set itself contains averageRating and reviewsCount. Lowercasing input before case-sensitive membership makes those intended values impossible to accept.

The contract's JSON-format example contains object and array values, matching the converter's parsed JSON nodes. The shared string-only ConsumerRecord value schema contradicts those supported representations.
The existing-artifact fallback drops dryRun and ultimately calls version creation with false. A request explicitly promising no changes can therefore enter the persistent creation branch.
The schema's en example and ISO-639-1 description agree with the parser's en/cy codes. Its ENGLISH/WELSH enum incorrectly exposes language names instead of wire codes.
The contract distinguishes a designator mask for listing from an exact designator. The list handler reads the exact-designator key and ignores the advertised mask parameter.
The operation sends a generic device request and deliberately wraps its generic response for JSON. The command-output annotation references a different operation's response type.
The rating lookup route has incompatible segment orders in contract and implementation. Neither the supplied contract nor controller independently establishes which public path is intended.
⚠️ The numeric configuration property and update logic consistently use value. Declaring a numeric field named description in the request model misnames that setting.
⚠️ The inherited transplant API explicitly requires a valid expected hash to guard branch updates. The OpenAPI query annotation omits that requiredness.
Identifier lookup is a branch of the listing endpoint, yet it serializes a single identity directly. It should preserve the documented array shape for a matching singleton.
The method binds sortParam and sortDir but never applies them to its query. Only filtering, offset, and limit reach the service, so requested ordering is ignored.

⚠️ The parser deliberately converts metadata's direct entries into ExternalMetadata, with a key/value validation message. The generated schema exposes the internal wrapper as an extra nested metadata object.
